[[2014 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]] champions | bowl = [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | bowl_result = round of 64 }} {{2013–14 Mid-American Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2013–14 Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball team''' represented [[Western Michigan University]] (WMU) during the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Broncos were [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) overall and West Division co-champions with [[2013–14 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]], received the No. 1 seed in the [[2014 MAC men's basketball tournament|conference tournament]] and defeated Toledo in the conference finals to receive the MAC's automatic berth into the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. WMU is led by 11th year head coach [[Steve Hawkins]] and play their home games at [[University Arena (Western Michigan University)|University Arena]] in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]]. WMU was given a 14 seed in the NCAA Tournament and lost to No. 3 seeded [[2013–14 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] in the second round 77–53. Syracuse was ranked No. 14 in the [[AP Poll]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400546920|title=Syracuse clamps down on Western Michigan in blowout|website=ESPN|language=en|access-date=2022-05-21}} Seniors David Brown and [[Shayne Whittington]] were awarded All-MAC first team honors while Hawkins was awarded the MAC Coach of the Year. ==2013 recruiting class== Western Michigan brought in three freshmen from high school detailed in the following table. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Mario Matasovic | position = Power forward | hometown = Delafield, WI | highschool = [[St. John's Northwestern Military Academy|St. John's NW Military Academy]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 213 | commitdate = May 17, 2013 | scout stars = | rivals stars = | espn grade = 69 }} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Leo Svete | position = Small forward | hometown = Granger, IN | highschool = [[Penn High School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 188 | commitdate = July 6, 2012 | scout stars = 2 | rivals stars = | espn grade = 67 }} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Tucker Haymond | position = Shooting guard | hometown = Seattle, WA | highschool = [[Garfield High School (Seattle, Washington)|Garfield High School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 210 | commitdate = January 6, 2013 | scout stars = | rivals stars = | espn grade = }} {{College athlete recruit end | year = 2013 | rivals ref title = Rivals Western Michigan Basketball Commitment List | scout ref title = Scout Western Michigan Basketball Commitment List | espn ref title = ESPN Western Michigan Basketball Commitment List | rivals school = westernmichigan | scout s = 226 | espn schoolid = 2711 | scout overall = N/A | rivals overall = N/A | accessdate = January 13, 2014 | bball = yes }} ==Preseason== {| class="toccolours" style="float: left; margin-right: 1em;" cellspacing="2" ! Senior forward Shayne Whittington was selected to the West Division All-MAC Team. The Broncos did not receive any first place votes to win the division nor any votes to win the conference tournament. Western Michigan defeated [[Kalamazoo College]] 88–59{{cite web|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPID=1924&DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=209296978 |title=WMU Basketball vs. Kzoo College Stats |publisher=Wmubroncos.com |date=November 2, 2013 |accessdate=November 15, 2013}} and [[Aquinas College (Michigan)|Aquinas College]] 69–54{{cite web|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=24351&DB_LANG=C&SPID=1924&DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=209298527 |title=WMU–Aquinas Stats |publisher=Wmubroncos.com |date=November 4, 2013 |accessdate=November 15, 2013}} in exhibition games at University Arena prior to opening the regular season against [[2013–14 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team|New Mexico State]] in the Rainbow Classic. ==Season== ===Rainbow Classic=== Western Michigan opened the 2013–14 season in [[Hawaii]] by winning the Rainbow Classic. WMU finished 2–1 in the four-team, [[round-robin tournament]] along with New Mexico State and [[2013–14 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors basketball team|Hawai{{okina}}i]] and was awarded the title based on the tiebreaker of fewest points allowed in the tournament.{{cite web|url=http://www.nmstatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=1900&ATCLID=209305502 |title=NM State Men's Basketball Finish Outrigger Hotels and Resort Rainbow Classic Defeating Host Hawai'i, 95–88 |publisher=NMStateSports.com |date=November 12, 2013 |accessdate=November 15, 2013}} The Broncos gave up 194 total points while New Mexico State and Hawai{{okina}}i allowed 213 and 218 points, respectively. Senior guard David Brown was named to the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=209305483 |title=Broncos Close Rainbow Classic With Win Over Tigers |publisher=Wmubroncos.com |date=November 11, 2013 |accessdate=November 15, 2013}} ===Awards=== The Broncos received six MAC West Division Player of the Week awards this season. ====David Brown==== Senior guard David Brown was named the MAC West Division Player of the Week on February 10, 2014. In two wins over [[2013–14 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Ohio]] and [[2013–14 Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball team|Northern Illinois]], Brown averaged 23 [[point (basketball)|point]]s per game. Brown shot 14–23 (61%) for [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]]s and 10–14 (71%) on three-point field goals. He also had eight [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s and five [[steal (basketball)|steal]]s during the week. In the NIU game, Brown had 20 points in the first half while making his first nine shots of the game.{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/316327/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |title=MAC Announces Men's Basketball Players of the Week |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=February 10, 2014 |accessdate=February 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222211910/http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/316327/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} ====Connar Tava==== Sophomore forward Connar Tava was named the MAC West Division Player of the Week on December 2, 2013. Tava averaged 18 points, 10 rebounds, 3 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s and 2 steals in a 99–88 win over [[2013–14 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]] and an 83–70 win over [[2013–14 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team|Cornell]].{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/News/tabid/969/Article/294264/ohios-ndour-wmus-tava-named-mac-basketball-players-of-the-week.aspx |title=Ohio's Ndour, WMU's Tava Named MAC Basketball Players of the Week |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=December 2, 2013 |accessdate=December 10, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131212175617/http://www.mac-sports.com/News/tabid/969/Article/294264/ohios-ndour-wmus-tava-named-mac-basketball-players-of-the-week.aspx |archive-date=December 12, 2013 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} Tava made all eight field goal attempts against Oakland and recorded his first career [[double–double]] against Cornell. Tava won his second MAC West Division Player of the Week on January 13, 2014. In two victories over preseason favorite [[2013–14 Toledo Rockets men's basketball team|Toledo]] and [[2013–14 Miami RedHawks men's basketball team|Miami]], Tava averaged 23.5 points per game and made 16 of 17 field goals (94.1%). The only field goal he missed was his final shot of the game against Miami. Tava also recorded nine rebounds, six assists, two [[blocked shot]]s and two steals during the two games.{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/307071/Akron-s-Diggs-Western-Michigan-s-Tava-Claim-Weekly-Honors.aspx |title=Akron's Diggs, Western Michigan's Tava Claim Weekly Honors |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=January 13, 2014 |accessdate=January 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140113210431/http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/307071/Akron-s-Diggs-Western-Michigan-s-Tava-Claim-Weekly-Honors.aspx |archive-date=January 13, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} ====Shayne Whittington==== Senior center Shayne Whittington was named the MAC West Division Player of the Week on January 27, 2014. Whittington averaged 19.5 points, 10.5 rebounds and 1.5 blocked shots per game in two wins against [[2013–14 Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball team|Kent State]] and [[2013–14 Ball State Cardinals men's basketball team|Ball State]].{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/311560/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140127193733/http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/311560/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 27, 2014 |title=MAC Announces Men's Basketball Players of the Week |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=January 27, 2014 |accessdate=January 27, 2014 }} Whittington was named the co-MAC West Division Player of the Week on February 17, 2014. Whittington averaged 16.5 points and 8.5 rebounds per game in two wins over [[2013–14 Akron Zips men's basketball team|Akron]] and Miami that moved WMU into a tie for first place in the MAC. He also recorded four blocks against Miami.{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/319020/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |title=MAC Announces Men's Basketball Players of the Week |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=February 17, 2014 |accessdate=February 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222215342/http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/319020/MAC-Announces-Men-s-Basketball-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} He earned his second consecutive MAC West Player of the Week on February 24, 2014. In wins over Ohio and Eastern Michigan, Whittington averaged 16.5 points and 11.0 rebounds per game. He did that while missing two practices prior to the EMU game.{{cite web |url=http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/321672/UB-s-McCrea-WMU-s-Whittington-Named-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |title=UB's McCrea, WMU's Whittington Named Players of the Week |publisher=Mid-American Conference |date=February 24, 2014 |accessdate=February 24, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228122426/http://www.mac-sports.com/tabid/969/Article/321672/UB-s-McCrea-WMU-s-Whittington-Named-Players-of-the-Week.aspx |archive-date=February 28, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} ==Roster== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !
